(Los Angeles, California) | college = [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] (2021–2024) | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2023–24 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2024]]) * Second-team All-Pac-12 ([[2022–23 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2023]]) * [[Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team (2022) }} '''Kenneth "KJ" Simpson Jr.''' (born August 8, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Simpson grew up in [[Panorama City, Los Angeles]] and attended [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (California)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/11/11/signing-day-chaminades-kj-simpson-keith-higgins-accomplish-childhood-dream-together/|title=Signing Day: Chaminade’s KJ Simpson, Keith Higgins accomplish childhood dream together|work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]|date=November 11, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2024}} He was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and initially committed to playing college basketball for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/four-star-guard-k-j-simpson-commits-to-arizona-wildcats/article_52436614-df42-11ea-9d40-cf3c32cc1c49.html|title=Four-star guard K.J. Simpson commits to Arizona Wildcats|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=August 15, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2024}} After Arizona head coach [[Sean Miller]] was fired, Simpson requested and was granted a release from his [[National Letter of Intent]] and reopened his recruitment.{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-signee-kj-simpson-to-look-elsewhere-after-receiving-release-from-letter-of-intent/article_9d07118a-a17c-11eb-9cd3-cb19e0300a48.html|title=Arizona signee KJ Simpson to look elsewhere after receiving release from letter-of-intent|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=January 11, 2024}} He ultimately signed to play at [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/k-j-simpson-commitment-university-colorado-boulder-buffaloes/|title=Four-Star Recruit K.J. Simpson Gives Commitment To CU Buffs|website=[[KCNC-TV|CBS News Colorado]]|date=April 28, 2021|access-date=January 11, 2024}} ==College career== Simpson was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference]] All-Freshman team during his first season playing for the Colorado Buffaloes after averaging 7.4 points per game and also leading the team in total assists and steals.{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/10/24/tristan-da-silva-kj-simpson-earn-pac-12-mbb-preseason-all-conference-honors/|title=CU Buffs’ Tristan da Silva, KJ Simpson earn Pac-12 MBB preseason all-conference honors|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=January 11, 2024}} He was named second-team All-Pac-12 after averaging 15.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.5 steals per game as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/college-basketball-players-colorado-rankings-cbs-sports-list-best-mens/|title=4 basketball players in Colorado make CBS Sports list of nation's best men's college hoopers|first=Jesse|last=Sarles|website=[[KCNC-TV|CBS News Colorado]]|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2024}} As a junior, Simpson was named to the first-team All-Pac-12, averaging a team-high 19.7 points per game and shooting 43% from three-point range this season.{{cite web |last1=camellis |title=Colorado’s KJ Simpson named to first team All Pac-12 |url=https://www.ralphiereport.com/2024/3/12/24099127/colorados-kj-simpson-named-to-first-team-all-pac-12 |website=ralphiereport.com |access-date=March 22, 2024}} In the first round of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA tournament]] against No. 7 [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], Simpson hit a game-winning jumper with less than two seconds left to secure a 102–100 victory.{{cite web |last1=Owens |first1=Jason |title=March Madness: No. 10 Colorado holds for 102-100 thriller over Florida on late KJ Simpson game winner |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/march-madness-no-10-colorado-holds-for-102-100-thriller-over-florida-on-late-kj-simpson-game-winner-230913474.html? |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=March 22, 2024}}
